lead.headline: IBM puts a hard disk in the personal-computer aisle
lead.dek: On March 8, IBM introduced the Personal Computer XT, an expanded PC with a 10 MB fixed disk that made the office micro feel more permanent.
lead.body: During the week of March 7-13, 1983, IBM gave business buyers a clearer upgrade path from the original PC. Contemporary coverage described the PC XT as a new model with more expansion room and a built-in fixed disk, while the quoted $4,995 configuration kept it firmly in office-machine territory. The timing helped software such as Lotus 1-2-3 look less like an add-on and more like the daily reason to buy an IBM-compatible desk system.
